summary: The repository and package layout is close to implementable; the biggest gaps are whether kyyn-surfaces or kyyn owns transport IO and which package holds the shared wire profile, plus the plugins/files naming conflict.

questions.text: ADR 0026 places the first-party file sink in plugins/files/, while ADRs 0015 and 0017 make it part of the local-file plugin alongside the folder source.
questions.reason: The plugin name fixes generated modules, config file and SinkReference, and one package versus two; 0026 'files/ First-party file sink' vs 0017 'The local-file plugin supplies the file sink alongside its existing source' and 0015 'plugins/local-file'.

questions.text: Does kyyn-surfaces perform transport IO (HTTP listener, MCP stdio loop, terminal input), or only pure parsing and rendering with IO in kyyn?
questions.reason: It decides which package depends on server and stdio libraries and how import checks are written; 0003 'Transport IO belongs in adapters' and 0026 'kyyn-surfaces CLI, MCP and HTTP adapters' vs 0018 'parsing and pure rendering live in kyyn-surfaces'.

questions.text: Which package holds the shared Kyyn.Types.* wire profile and generated-codec support used by host and guest runtime?
questions.reason: It sets the Cabal graph, MicroHs build inputs and what the SDK catalogue excludes; 0026 'Leave the exact shared wire-type/codec package placement to ADR 0007', and ADR 0007 selects libraries without naming a package.

questions.text: Are json-0.11, transformers, haskell-agentic and the native provider packages vendored under vendor/ like MicroHs, or resolved as Cabal dependencies?
questions.reason: Guest libraries ship as source and native builds must work from a source archive; 0007, 0020 and 0028 cite sources 'recorded in vendored inputs', but 0026's layout shows only vendor/MicroHs/ and native provider packages are not covered.
